messages.subject: Re: design of sampling units
parts:
Hi Ricardo, list,

What you are proposing (post-stratifing the transects into many strata, each
of which has a unique combination of the factors of interest) is a design-
based approach to answering your question. It is not an ideal approach in
your case for several reasons:
- the transects were not laid down at random- you have few transects and
relatively little survey effort
- there are several factors, so there will be many strata each of which will
contain little (or maybe no) survey effort
- the analysis will be complex as you will need to deal with correlation
between strata due to splitting the same transects into different strata

Instead, can I suggest you take a model-based approach, where you construct
a statistical model to explain density/abundance in terms of the factors of
interest. A model based approach doesn't make any assumption about the
design, so non-random transects are not necessarily a problem (although they
can cause other issues such as non-uniform distribution of animals with
respect to the transect line). Model selection methods also allow you to
directly address the question of interest: what factors affect animal
density. One downside is that the analysis methods are not simple.

Some approaches to model-basd estimation are given in Chapter 4 of the
Advanced Distance Sampling book, and also in
Hedley, S.L., Buckland, S.T. and Borchers, D.L. 1999. Spatial modelling from
line transect data. Journal of Cetacean Research and Management 1, 255-264.

We are currently developing an analysis engine in Distance that implements
the "count" method described in the book chapter, and will provide training
on this method and a beta version of the analysis engine in our up-coming
workshop at St Andrews this summer "Primer on Density Surface Modelling from
Distance Sampling Data" - for more on this, see
http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance.workshops/
We don't have a timetable for a public release of the new analysis engine
yet I'm afraid.

Others are using and developing similar approaches (which are also sometimes
called "spatial modelling" or "density surface modelling") - for some clues
try searching the distance-sampling list using the key word "spatial".

Hope this helps,

- Len

On Wed, 12 Apr 2006 19:27:08 -0300, Ricardo Baldi wrote:

> >Dear all,

> >We are surveying the population of guanacos (a large, wild ungulate)
> >in a 3600 km2 island-like peninsula in eastern Patagonia, aiming to
> >explain the variation in abundance due to habitat and human-related
> >factors. We surveyed 360 km of transects, using internal "roads"
> >(usually very bad, always surveyed using a 4WD pickup vehicle)
> >connecting different ranches across the area. In total, we traveled
> >along 12 different lines of variable length (between 9 and 70 km).
> >The explanatory factors (each with 3 levels) we are considering are:
> >habitat type, density of ranch-buildings and hunting pressure. Sheep
> >abundance will be an explanatory variable based on the estimates of
> >sheep encounter rate. The response variable will be guanaco encounter
> >rate.
> >As we will combine the factors with their different levels, this will
> >result in 9 different strata. Thus, we will consider the sampling
> >unit for a given stratum as the part of a long transect falling
> >within that stratum. Our problem is that the number of sampling units
> >per stratum will be too small in relation to the number of
> >explanatory variables/factors we want to test.
> >Questions are:
> >1. Is it valid to split the transect into smaller segments along a
> >line, and to consider these smaller segments as the new sampling
> >units?
> >If so, we may now face the problem of autocorrelation among the
> >sampling units placed along the same transect.
> >2. Is it possible to solve this problem by separating the new
> >sampling units, leaving blank spaces between them?
> >3. If this is ok, how can we detect and measure the autocorrelation
> >between smaller sampling units in order to decide their length and
> >the separation between contiguous units?

> >Any help/suggestions will be very much appreciated-

> >Ricardo
